title: Goal-oriented learning of stochastic differential equations using error bounds on path-space observables
summary: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs), which serve as the governing equations for dynamical systems in a broad range of applications, can become cost-prohibitive for numerical simulation at scales necessary for quantifying key properties. Surrogate models of the drift function of an SDE, learned from data of the high-fidelity system, are routinely used to increase the efficiency of simulation and prediction of properties.
